frequency_question: How often does a motivated faction in Congress succeed in passing a joint resolution of disapproval through both chambers to block a major international agreement within the statutory review window?
membership_rule: Includes formal joint resolutions of disapproval targeting major nuclear or high-stakes defense agreements introduced under statutory review mechanisms; excludes non-binding resolutions of inquiry or simple resolutions.

cases.name: Saudi Arabia arms sales disapproval (Trump era)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 major historical attempts identified where Congress attempted statutory blocking of executive international agreements; all failed to achieve final veto-proof enactment.
known_gaps: Minor informal disapproval resolutions omitted as they lack statutory blocking teeth.
skeleton: Legislative sessions with high-stakes executive agreement reviews × historical success rate of overriding executive will on foreign policy agreements
multiplier: 4 historical major attempts / 0 successful final veto-proof blockages
validity_reason: The institutional balance of power between the executive and legislative branches on foreign agreements governed by the AECA or similar statutes remains stable over multi-decade horizons.
